content.content:
`deccy discard <handle>...` discards one open draft per handle named. The invocation names one or more handles and nothing else; each handle picks out one draft's record, and the call ends that draft without landing it. The call writes no node and no change, and it is not one of the three operations. What becomes of the record document, of the draft's workspace and its directory, and of the change the draft's workspace holds belongs to the commitments this surface names and does not restate.

The verb is `discard`, a single lowercase word in the verb position, and everything after it is that verb's arguments (wzmmmmsw). It is the only spelling of its purpose: ending an open draft without landing it — the end tvxspkyy settles — is served by `discard` and by no other verb, and v1 has no aliases (znkxvuyv). Opening a draft, landing one, and removing a node are other purposes, each served by its own verb (znkxvuyv); a caller who reaches for `discard` to mean one of them has named the wrong verb, not found a second spelling of it.

The form takes a positional list of one or more handles, and its argument surface is answered before anything else is reached. Every verb answers its argument surface before it reaches for the workspace, refusing there — naming it — a missing required argument and an argument the form does not name (qtqnuqxo). This form's required argument is the handle list, so a call naming no handle is refused at that point, before the store is consulted and before any workspace is reached, since with no handle there is no key to look up in the directory the records are found in (qtqnuqxo, twpvqstu). The surface does not judge the handles themselves: a handle is a well-formed argument whatever it names, so no handle is refused at the argument surface, and whether it picks out an open record is a question answered from the store afterwards (qtqnuqxo, owyntkvw). What a refusal says, where it writes and what it exits with are not this surface's to fix; what is fixed is that a malformed call is refused at the argument surface rather than by a root-less context or a missing workspace (qtqnuqxo).

The handle is the only key that addresses a draft. A record's identity is the handle minted for the draft and written into it as its key, so the record is the thing that key picks out, while the target node, the edit and the workspace are references the record carries and not keys (owyntkvw). `discard` therefore reads its arguments as handles: one handle names one record and therefore one draft, and a handle repeated in one call names the same draft, which the call discards once (owyntkvw). Nothing else addresses a draft. A node id is not an address — the node is a reference a record carries, and one node may be named by several records at once (owyntkvw) — so a node id is read as a key that picks out no record; the call asks the store for a record at that key, a handle the directory does not name is a record that is not there (twpvqstu), and the call is refused with nothing discarded. Several drafts of one node — competing alternatives within one edit, or a redraft beside an open one — are therefore discarded one handle at a time: each draft has its own handle and its own record, and no argument can name the drafts of a node or of an edit as a set (owyntkvw). A call names handles, so each of those drafts is discarded only by a call that names its handle.

Only an open record is a subject. A record has exactly two states — `open` for a draft that has not landed and `landed` for one that has — the only transition is `open` → `landed` made at the landing, and `landed` is terminal (tvxspkyy). The store retains a landed record at its handle, and a handle the directory does not name is a record that is not there (twpvqstu). The handles a call can discard are therefore exactly the open records it names. A handle whose record has landed names a draft that cannot be discarded, and a handle the store does not hold names no record at all; in either case the call is refused and nothing is discarded — not that handle's draft and not the drafts named beside it. Nothing is discarded by a refused call: no draft is ended and no record turns from open to landed (tvxspkyy, twpvqstu).

The refusal is the call's, and one invocation answers once. An invocation is one verb with its arguments (wzmmmmsw), so a call is either answered with the discards it names or refused; it is never answered half way, with the open handles discarded and the rest refused. The rule follows from the subject set rather than standing beside it: the call's subject is one open draft per handle (owyntkvw), and a handle that names no open record gives the call no such subject (tvxspkyy, twpvqstu), so a call carrying that handle names a set it cannot answer and is refused whole, with nothing discarded. Which handles a refusal reports, in what words and on what stream, belongs to the refusal layer; the surface fixes only that the call is refused and that none of the drafts it named was discarded.

A drifted draft is still a subject, and drift is not a refusal. A drifted draft — an open record whose workspace jj no longer has — is still an open draft (tvxspkyy), so it is a subject like any other. The surface decides whether a handle is a subject by reading the record's state and not by consulting the workspace: the question it answers is whether the record is open, and whether the workspace is still there is not part of that question (tvxspkyy). So a call naming a drifted draft is answered as a discard of that draft and is not refused because of the drift, and the surface adds no check that a workspace exists before it accepts a handle. What the discard then does at the workspace or at its directory is the workspace commitment's to say and is not settled here (vzposmvm).

The call writes no node and no change, and it is not an operation. A discard creates no node and no change, opens no bracket, writes no marker, and offers undo and redo no unit (tvxspkyy). The change-side act behind a discard — what becomes of the change the draft's workspace holds — is vxltqruo's; this surface neither restates it nor widens it, and it writes no node and no change itself. Nor does this surface restate the store's side or the workspace's: what becomes of the discarded draft's record document, of every other record and of a later scan is the store's removal (twpvqstu), and what becomes of the draft's workspace and its directory is the workspace half (vzposmvm). What this surface settles is which invocations are answered with a discard and which are refused; carrying each discard out is theirs.

These clauses are one commitment, not a list of rules about different things. Take the verb away and there is no invocation; let a second spelling serve the purpose and `discard` is an alias, which v1 has none of (znkxvuyv); answer the argument surface late and an empty call reaches the store before it is refused (qtqnuqxo); let a node or an edit address the draft and the handle stops being the key (owyntkvw); drop the open-only subject and a landed record becomes the discarded subject although it is terminal; let the call answer partly and one invocation has two answers (wzmmmmsw); drop drift from the subject set and the surface refuses a draft the lifecycle still holds open (tvxspkyy); let the call write a node or a change and discarding becomes a fourth operation (tvxspkyy). They answer one question — which invocations discard a draft, and which are refused — with one answer: `deccy discard <handle>...`, one open draft per handle, refused whole when any handle names no open record, and no node or change written.

Deliberately not here. The store's removal — the document, its path, the scan that finds the rest and the retention of every other record — and the record's fields and version (twpvqstu); the draft's workspace forget, the directory removal, and how an absence at either point is treated (vzposmvm); which change a discard gives up and by what invocation and flags (vxltqruo); the success output, the refusal's wording, stream and exit status, and the help text; the removal guard's rule, which is another commitment's and not an edge of this one; what a handle looks like and how it is minted; and whether a well-formed call needs a repository root, which is the operation's question rather than this surface's (qtqnuqxo). Each can change without touching what is settled here: one verb, a list of handles, one open draft per handle, refused whole when any handle names no open record, and no node or change written.
content.rationale:
This node is prose because the commitment is the shape of the invocation that discards a draft — the verb, the arguments it takes, and the calls it does not answer with a discard — and every one of its eight prerequisites is prose; each edge is a natural-to-natural reading, answered by reading the clauses against the recorded decisions, with nothing to run.

The surface is stated once and then read where it could be mistaken. One verb, `discard`, a single lowercase word with everything after it its arguments (wzmmmmsw), serving the one purpose tvxspkyy settles and no second spelling of it (znkxvuyv). The arguments are one or more handles, and the argument surface is answered first: an empty call is refused there, before the store is read or a workspace reached (qtqnuqxo), and a handle is well formed whatever it names, so no handle is refused at that point and whether it picks out an open record is a store question answered afterwards (owyntkvw, twpvqstu). The handle is the only address because it is the record's identity while the node, the edit and the workspace are references and one node may be named by several records (owyntkvw); a node id is therefore looked up as a key that names no record and refused (twpvqstu), and a node's several drafts are discarded one handle at a time. The subject is the open record and only that: landed is terminal and never discarded, and a handle the directory does not name is not a record (tvxspkyy, twpvqstu), so both are refused with nothing discarded. The refusal is the call's because an invocation is one verb with its arguments (wzmmmmsw) and the subject set is the drafts its handles name (owyntkvw), so a call carrying a handle that names no open record is refused whole. Drift does not shrink the subject set, because a drifted draft is still an open draft (tvxspkyy), and the surface reads the record's state rather than the workspace; what the discard does at the workspace or at its directory is vzposmvm's and is not stated here. And the call writes no node and no change and is not an operation (tvxspkyy), with the change-side act left to vxltqruo.

Each clause names the prerequisite its soundness rests on, read off what the clause says rather than off its citation: the one-verb form and one answer per invocation rest on wzmmmmsw; the single spelling and the absence of aliases on znkxvuyv; the argument surface answered first on qtqnuqxo; the handle as the only key, the node and edit as references, and several drafts under one node on owyntkvw; the handle-named document, the absence of a record at an unknown handle, and the retention of landed records on twpvqstu; the two states, the terminal landed end, the open-only subject, the drifted draft still open, and the absence of any node or change written on tvxspkyy; the workspace half on vzposmvm; and the change-side act on vxltqruo.

The scope stops where other commitments begin, and the node says so rather than deciding them: the store's removal, the workspace and directory mechanics including how an absence at either point is treated, the change-side act and its invocation and flags, the output, refusal wording, exit status and help text, the removal guard's rule, the handle's format, and the root requirement of a well-formed call are recorded elsewhere and are not edges of this one. Each could change without the surface changing, and the surface could change without them.

Red is the node's absence: the skeleton states no clause of a verb surface and names no prerequisite, so there is no commitment for criteria 1–3 to read. The check is a review of the two node documents; no command runs, and the findings are the reviewer's.
